en: to be speckled black; to be blackish

examples.ko: 며칠 면도를 안 했더니 턱이 거뭇거뭇해요.
examples.en: I haven't shaved for a few days, so my chin is shadowed with stubble.
Dark spots have appeared on the banana.
My son's upper lip has started to get a dark shadow.
The wall got stained with dark patches of mold.

examples.ko: 감자 껍질이 거뭇거뭇해서 다 깎아 냈어요.
examples.en: The potato skin had dark spots, so I peeled it all off.
The sky grew dark in patches and then a shower poured down.

explain: 여기저기 검은 것이 조금씩 보이거나 군데군데 어둡게 보일 때 써요. 수염이 막 자랄 때나 과일에 점이 생길 때 잘 어울려요. 전체가 고르게 어두운 '거무스름하다'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: The wall became dotted with dark patches from mold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군데군데 검게 변해 가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes things turning dark in patches.

phrases.en: His beard started to come in as dark stubble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수염이나 털이 막 자랄 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for when a beard or hair is just starting to grow.

phrases.en: In the photo, the face looks speckled with dark spots.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해 보이다'를 붙여 눈에 보이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-해 보이다' describes how something looks.

explain_en: Use it when dark bits show up here and there, or patches look dim. It suits fresh stubble or spots on fruit. It differs from '거무스름하다', which describes an even darkness overall.

examples.ko: 기초화장을 먼저 하고 색조 화장을 해요.
examples.en: I do my skincare base first and then color makeup.
I only do the basic skincare step before going out.
Your makeup won't flake if your base skincare goes on well.
My skin is dry, so I pay attention to my base skincare.

examples.ko: 기초화장은 보통 스킨, 로션 순서로 해요.
examples.en: For basic skincare you usually go in the order of toner then lotion.
I bought new basic skincare products.

explain: 스킨, 로션, 크림처럼 피부를 정리하는 단계를 말해요. 색을 입히는 '색조 화장'과 짝으로 말하고, 보통 기초화장을 먼저 해요.

phrases.en: I bought new basic skincare products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스킨, 로션, 크림 같은 제품 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the products themselves, like toner, lotion and cream.

phrases.en: I do my basic skincare carefully in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부를 정리하는 단계를 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Doing the skin-prep step.

phrases.en: I finished my basic skincare and put on sunscreen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다음 단계로 넘어가기 전에 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before moving on to the next step.

explain_en: It refers to the skin-prep step with toner, lotion and cream. It is paired with '색조 화장' (color makeup), and you usually do the base skincare first.

examples.en: My face feels tight after I wash it.

examples.ko: 운동 후에 허벅지가 땅겨서 계단이 힘들어요.
examples.en: My thighs feel tight after exercise, so stairs are hard.
The surgery site feels tight and pulled.
My lips feel tight and crack because they are dry.

examples.ko: 팩을 하면 피부가 땅길 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes my skin feels tight when I use a face mask.

examples.ko: 자고 일어났더니 목이 땅기면 스트레칭을 해 보세요.
examples.en: If your neck feels tight after waking up, try stretching.

explain: 피부나 근육이 팽팽하게 당겨지는 듯 불편한 느낌에 써요. 줄을 당기거나 '입맛이 당기다'처럼 말할 때는 '당기다'를 써요. 주로 '얼굴이 땅기다', '다리가 땅기다'처럼 몸의 부분이 주어가 돼요.

phrases.en: In winter the air is dry, so my skin feels tight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부가 건조해서 당기는 느낌일 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when dry skin feels tight.

phrases.example: 오래 걸었더니 종아리가 땅겨서 쉬고 싶어요.
phrases.en: After walking for a long time, my calves feel tight and I want to rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 근육 부위가 팽팽하게 아플 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a muscle area feels taut and sore.

phrases.en: I feel a pulling sensation around the wound.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 증상을 설명할 때 써요. 병원에서 말하기 좋은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form is useful for describing symptoms, such as at a clinic.

explain_en: It describes the uncomfortable feeling of skin or muscles being stretched tight. For pulling a rope or for '입맛이 당기다' (to have an appetite for something), use '당기다' instead. The subject is usually a body part, like '얼굴이 땅기다' or '다리가 땅기다'.

en: to have one's eyes wide open

examples.ko: 낮잠을 길게 잤더니 밤에도 정신이 말똥말똥해요.
examples.en: I took a long nap, so my mind is wide awake even at night.
The child's eyes are wide open, so it's hard to get him to sleep.
It was the night before the exam and I was nervous, so my mind was wide awake.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 말똥말똥하던 아이가 갑자기 졸았어요.
examples.en: The kid who was alert in class suddenly dozed off.

examples.ko: 아기 눈이 말똥말똥하니까 아직 안 졸린가 봐요.
examples.en: The baby's eyes are wide open, so he must not be sleepy yet.

examples.ko: 졸릴 줄 알았는데 오히려 눈이 말똥말똥하게 떠졌어요.
examples.en: I thought I'd be sleepy, but my eyes actually popped wide open.

explain: '눈이/정신이 말똥말똥하다'처럼 눈이나 정신이 또렷하게 깨어 있을 때 써요. 졸리거나 피곤한 상태와 반대이고, 자야 할 때 잠이 안 오는 상황에서 특히 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I drank coffee, so my mind is wide awake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어를 해요체로 바꾼 형태로, 지금 정신이 또렷하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite 해요 form, used to say your mind is alert right now.

phrases.en: He looks at the teacher with bright, wide-open eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔서 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form, used to modify the noun that follows.

phrases.en: My eyes are wide open, so I can't fall asleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아서/어서'로 이유를 붙여 잠이 안 오는 상황을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a reason with '-아서/어서'; commonly used when you can't fall asleep.

explain_en: It is used like '눈이/정신이 말똥말똥하다' when the eyes or mind are clearly awake. It is the opposite of sleepy or tired, and comes up especially when you should be sleeping but can't.

en: to be nauseated; to be sick; to be nauseating

examples.en: I feel sick because of motion sickness.

examples.ko: 빈속에 약을 먹으면 속이 메스꺼울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Taking medicine on an empty stomach can make you nauseous.
When I see blood I feel sick, so I close my eyes.

examples.ko: 어제 먹은 음식이 안 맞았는지 속이 메스꺼웠어요.
examples.en: Maybe the food I ate yesterday didn't agree with me, I felt nauseous.

examples.ko: 속이 메스껍고 어지러워서 일찍 집에 갔어요.
examples.en: I felt sick and dizzy, so I went home early.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 거짓말은 듣기만 해도 메스꺼워요.
examples.en: That person's lies make me sick just to hear.

explain: 토할 것 같은 속의 느낌이에요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라서 '메스꺼워요, 메스꺼운'으로 바뀌고 '매스껍다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 자꾸 속이 불편할 때는 '메슥거리다', 배가 흔들리듯 불편할 때는 '울렁거리다'가 잘 맞아요.

phrases.en: The smell is so strong that I feel nauseous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 '메스껍다'가 '메스꺼워요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the ㅂ irregular, 'meseukkeopda' becomes 'meseukkeowoyo'.

phrases.en: I get a nauseous feeling when I ride in a car.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느낌이 들다'와 함께 몸 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'neukkimi deulda' to describe how your body feels.

phrases.en: My stomach doesn't feel nauseous anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙여서 속이 괜찮아졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-ji anta', it means your stomach feels fine now.

explain_en: It is the feeling of being about to throw up. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective (메스꺼워요, 메스꺼운), and '매스껍다' is used with the same meaning. '메슥거리다' fits a repeatedly upset stomach, and '울렁거리다' fits a queasy, rolling feeling.

examples.en: I gently cleaned my ear with a cotton swab.
I bought a box of cotton swabs at the pharmacy.

examples.ko: 상처에 약을 바를 때 면봉이 편해요.
examples.en: A cotton swab is handy for putting medicine on a wound.

examples.ko: 화장할 때 면봉으로 번진 곳을 고쳐요.
examples.en: When doing makeup, I fix smudges with a cotton swab.
It is dangerous to put a cotton swab in too deep.
I throw used cotton swabs in the trash.

explain: 작은 막대 끝에 솜을 감은 물건이에요. 귀를 닦거나 약을 바를 때, 화장 고칠 때 써요. 코로나 검사에서 검체를 얻는 긴 막대는 '검체 채취용 면봉'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I applied the medicine to the wound with a cotton swab.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약이나 화장품을 조금만 바를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when applying just a little medicine or makeup.

phrases.en: I put disposable cotton swabs in my travel bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 쓰고 버리는 면봉을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Swabs that are thrown away after one use.

phrases.en: I have a box of cotton swabs at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 통에 든 면봉을 '한 통', '두 통'처럼 셀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Swabs sold in a small container are counted as 한 통, 두 통, and so on.

explain_en: A small stick with cotton wrapped at the end. It is used to clean ears, apply medicine and fix makeup. The long stick used to collect samples in COVID tests is called a 검체 채취용 면봉.

examples.en: Ramie clothes are cool, so they are nice in summer.
My grandmother ironed her ramie clothes neatly and wore them.
You have to be careful when washing ramie clothes.

examples.ko: 한복 가게에서 모시옷도 맞출 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard you can also have ramie clothes made at the hanbok shop.

examples.ko: 모시옷 입은 어르신이 마루에 앉아 계셨어요.
examples.en: An elder in ramie clothes was sitting on the porch.

examples.ko: 어머니께서 모시옷으로 만든 여름 한복을 선물받으셨어요.
examples.en: My mother received a summer hanbok made of ramie as a gift.

explain: '모시'라는 풀의 껍질로 짠 얇고 시원한 천으로 만든 옷이에요. 바람이 잘 통해서 여름 한복에 많이 써요. 구김이 잘 가서 조심해서 다뤄야 한다고 해요.

phrases.en: Wearing ramie clothes on a hot day keeps you cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입는 행동을 말할 때 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for wearing the clothes.

phrases.en: I ironed my ramie clothes before going out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구김이 잘 가는 옷이라 다림질 이야기와 자주 같이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears with ironing because the fabric wrinkles easily.

phrases.en: Summer ramie clothes let the breeze through well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절과 함께 써서 여름용 옷이라는 것을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with the season to show it is summer wear.

explain_en: It is clothing made of a thin, cool fabric woven from the fiber of the ramie plant (모시). It lets air through well, so it is commonly used for summer hanbok. People say it wrinkles easily and needs careful handling.

examples.en: In winter a wool coat is nice because it's warm.

examples.ko: 이 정장은 모직이라서 세탁소에 맡겨야 해요.
examples.en: This suit is wool, so I have to take it to the dry cleaner.

examples.ko: 모직은 보풀이 잘 생겨서 관리가 필요해요.
examples.en: Wool pills easily, so it needs care.

examples.ko: 어머니가 모직으로 된 치마를 사 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother bought me a skirt made of wool.

examples.ko: 모직과 면 중에서 어느 것이 더 따뜻해요?
examples.en: Which is warmer, wool or cotton?

examples.ko: 이 목도리는 모직 백 퍼센트라서 아주 따뜻해요.
examples.en: This scarf is 100 percent wool, so it's very warm.

explain: 양털로 짠 천을 말하고, 영어에서 온 '울'이라고도 해요. 보통 '모직 코트', '모직 양복'처럼 옷 이름 앞에 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: This coat is 100% wool, so it's warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모직'과 같은 뜻의 영어에서 온 말로, 옷 상표나 가게에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An English loanword with the same meaning as 모직, often seen on clothing labels and in shops.

phrases.en: My father went to work wearing a wool suit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모직' 뒤에 옷 이름을 붙여 어떤 천으로 만든 옷인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting a clothing word after 모직 tells what fabric the item is made of.

phrases.en: This scarf is made of wool, so it's warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 재료가 모직이라고 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that an item's material is wool.

explain_en: It means cloth woven from sheep's wool, and people also say '울' (from English 'wool'). It is usually placed before a clothing item, as in '모직 코트' or '모직 양복'.

en: to be smooth; to be sleek

examples.ko: 새로 나온 자동차는 디자인이 미끈하게 빠졌어요.
examples.en: The new car has a sleek design.
That model has long, shapely legs.

examples.ko: 미끈한 종아리 아래에 검은 구두가 반짝였어요.
examples.en: Black shoes shone beneath her smooth, slender calves.
Once I peeled it, the inside turned out smooth.
The ice is slick, so it's hard to walk.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 껍질을 벗기면 미끈하고 단단해요.
examples.en: Once you peel off the bark, this wood is smooth and hard.

explain: 거친 데 없이 매끄럽고 시원스럽게 잘 빠진 모습을 말해요. 다리, 몸매, 자동차 디자인 같은 것을 칭찬할 때도 쓰고, 얼음처럼 미끄러운 표면에도 써요. 어떤 뜻인지는 문장 속 대상을 보고 구분해요.

phrases.en: That actress is famous for her sleek figure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군살 없이 잘 빠진 몸을 칭찬하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for a trim, well-proportioned figure.

phrases.en: This car has a sleek design.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빠지다'와 함께 모양이 시원스럽게 잘 만들어졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 빠지다, it means well and cleanly shaped.

phrases.en: The sleek car body really catches the eye.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 물건의 매끄러운 겉모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the smooth outer look of machines or objects.

explain_en: It describes something smooth with no rough spots and nicely shaped. People use it to compliment legs, figures or car designs, and also for slick surfaces like ice. Check the object in the sentence to tell which meaning is intended.

examples.en: It was hot, so I wore a sleeveless T-shirt.

examples.ko: 민소매 원피스는 회사에서 입기 조금 부담돼요.
examples.en: A sleeveless dress feels a bit awkward to wear to the office.
I put a thin cardigan over my sleeveless top.

examples.ko: 이 민소매는 여름에 입기 정말 시원해요.
examples.en: This sleeveless top is really cool to wear in summer.
My arms feel cool in a sleeveless top.

examples.ko: 동생이 민소매 차림으로 나가서 감기에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling went out in a sleeveless outfit and caught a cold.

explain: '민-'은 장식이나 덮는 것이 없다는 느낌을 더해요. 그래서 민소매는 소매가 없는 옷이고, 민얼굴, 민무늬도 같은 방식이에요. 영어의 '나시'는 일본식 표현이라 요즘은 '민소매'라고 하는 게 더 바른 말이에요.

phrases.en: In summer I often wear sleeveless tops.
phrases.nuance_ko: '티셔츠'를 빼고 '민소매'만 말해도 옷을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: '민소매' alone can refer to the garment without saying 'T-shirt'.

phrases.example: 민소매 옷은 시원해서 더운 날 좋아요.
phrases.en: Sleeveless clothes are cool, so they're good on hot days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소매가 없는 옷 전체를 넓게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broad term for any clothing without sleeves.

phrases.en: I put a thin cardigan over my sleeveless top.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실내가 추울 때 겹쳐 입는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes layering when indoors is cold.
phrases.en_equiv: a cardigan over a sleeveless top

explain_en: The prefix '민-' adds the sense of having nothing extra on it. So 민소매 is a garment with no sleeves, and 민얼굴 and 민무늬 work the same way. People also say '나시', a Japanese-origin word, but '민소매' is the standard Korean term.

en: to be greasy; to be glossy; to be lustrous

examples.en: I ate greasy food, so my lips are shiny with oil.
After I wiped the floor, it became glossy.
A child with a shiny face is smiling.
He put gel in his hair and combed it back sleekly.
The glossy shoes look brand new.
Your forehead is shiny from sweat.

explain: 기름기, 땀, 광택 때문에 표면이 윤이 나서 미끈해 보일 때 써요. '반짝반짝'은 깨끗하고 예쁜 느낌이 많지만, '번질번질'은 기름져 보이는 느낌이 있어서 때에 따라 덜 좋게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 젤을 많이 발라서 머리가 번질번질해 보여요.
phrases.en: I used a lot of gel, so my hair looks shiny and greasy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기름기로 윤이 나는 모습을 말하고, 덜 좋게 들릴 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a shine from oil, and can sound slightly negative.

phrases.en: I like this cream because it isn't greasy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기름져 보이지 않는다는 뜻으로 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says something does not look oily.

phrases.en: The new bag I bought is glossy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '번질번질하다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly interchangeable with 번질번질하다.

explain_en: It describes a surface that looks smooth and shiny because of oil, sweat or polish. '반짝반짝' often feels clean and pretty, but '번질번질' has a greasy look and can sometimes sound less positive.

examples.en: I cried all night, so my eyes are puffy.
Your face looks puffy; maybe you couldn't sleep.
I woke up in the morning with a puffy face and was startled.

examples.ko: 라면을 먹고 자면 다음 날 얼굴이 부석부석한 것 같아요.
examples.en: If I eat ramyeon and go to bed, my face seems puffy the next day.

examples.ko: 눈이 부석부석하면 찬 수건을 올려 보세요.
examples.en: If your eyes are puffy, try putting a cold towel on them.

examples.ko: 부석부석한 얼굴에 팩을 붙이고 잠깐 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I put a face mask on my puffy face and rested for a bit.

explain: 잠을 못 자거나 울거나 짜게 먹은 뒤에 얼굴이나 눈이 핏기 없이 부어 보일 때 써요. '푸석푸석하다'(거칠고 윤기가 없다)와 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 보통 '얼굴', '눈'과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I went to work with a puffy face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-한'을 붙여서 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -한 lets it modify a noun.

phrases.example: 어제 못 잤는지 눈이 부석부석해 보여요.
phrases.en: Your eyes look puffy, maybe because you didn't sleep yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something looks that way.

phrases.example: 라면을 먹고 잤더니 아침에 얼굴이 부석부석해졌어요.
phrases.en: I ate ramen and slept, so my face got puffy in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해지다'는 상태가 변했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: -해지다 shows a change of state.

explain_en: It describes a face or eyes that look swollen and pale, for example after missing sleep, crying or eating salty food. It sounds similar to '푸석푸석하다' (rough and dull), so it is easy to mix up. It is usually used with '얼굴' (face) and '눈' (eyes).

examples.en: The leaves have turned, so the mountain is dotted with red all over.
The mosquito bites are red and itchy.
Children run around among the red-dotted flower beds.
Red blotches came up on my face, so I went to a dermatologist.

examples.ko: 저녁 노을 때문에 바다가 불긋불긋해 보였어요.
examples.en: The sea looked patchy red because of the sunset.
The apples are ripening with red patches.

explain: '불긋불긋'은 부사이고 이 말은 형용사라서 '불긋불긋한 단풍'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸밀 수 있어요. 여러 색이 섞이면 '울긋불긋하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: As the weather got cold, the leaves turned reddish.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'를 붙여서 색이 변해 간다는 뜻을 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어지다 shows the color is changing.

phrases.en: The park is colorful with autumn leaves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 색이 섞여 있을 때는 '불긋불긋하다' 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this instead of 불긋불긋하다 when many colors are mixed.

phrases.example: 이제 모기에 물린 자리가 불긋불긋하지 않아요.
phrases.en: The mosquito bite is not red and spotty anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙여 부정할 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form using -지 않다.

explain_en: '불긋불긋' is an adverb, while this word is an adjective, so you can say '불긋불긋한 단풍' to modify a noun. When several colors are mixed, use '울긋불긋하다'.

examples.en: I bought a bikini for my summer vacation.

examples.ko: 그녀는 파란 비키니를 입고 바다로 갔어요.
examples.en: She went to the sea wearing a blue bikini.
I wore a thin shirt over my bikini.
I put the bikini in my bag.
This shop sells bikinis too.
The bikini got too small, so I have to buy a new one.

explain: 수영복은 '수영복'이 가장 일반적이고, '비키니'는 위아래가 나뉜 수영복만 가리켜요. 한 벌로 된 수영복은 보통 '원피스 수영복'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I took photos in a bikini at the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입는 동사 '입다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the clothing verb 입다.

phrases.example: 작년에 산 비키니 수영복이 아직 새것 같아요.
phrases.en: The bikini swimsuit I bought last year still looks new.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수영복' 앞에 붙여서 어떤 수영복인지 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting it before 수영복 makes clear which type of swimsuit.

phrases.en: I find a two-piece swimsuit more comfortable than a bikini.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위아래가 나뉜 수영복을 조금 더 넓게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader name for swimsuits with separate top and bottom.

explain_en: 수영복 is the general word for swimwear, while 비키니 means only the two-piece kind. A one-piece suit is usually called '원피스 수영복'.

examples.en: I put on lotion after washing up.
I packed my toiletries and went on a trip.
There are two washbasins in the bathroom.
In the morning I wash up and brush my teeth.
The hotel has toiletries prepared.

examples.ko: 세면할 때 물을 오래 틀어 두지 마세요.
examples.en: Do not leave the water running long when washing up.

explain: 혼자서는 잘 안 쓰고 '세면대', '세면도구' 같은 말에서 많이 봐요. 일상에서는 '세면했어요'보다 '세수했어요'라고 말해요. '세면'은 안내문이나 설명서에 나오는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I wash my hands at the sink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장실에서 씻는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the washbasin in a bathroom.

phrases.en: I put my toiletries in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칫솔, 비누처럼 씻을 때 쓰는 물건을 모두 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It covers items for washing, such as a toothbrush or soap.

explain_en: It rarely stands alone and appears in words like '세면대' and '세면도구'. In daily speech people say '세수했어요' rather than '세면했어요'. '세면' is a slightly formal word found in notices and manuals.

examples.en: At the bathhouse I got into the warm bath to loosen up.
I tried going back and forth between the hot and cold baths.

examples.ko: 온탕은 너무 뜨거워서 오래 못 있겠어요.
examples.en: The hot bath is so hot that I can't stay long.
The kids splashed around in the warm bath.

examples.ko: 피곤할 때는 온탕에 십 분쯤 몸을 담가요.
examples.en: When I'm tired, I soak in the warm bath for about ten minutes.

examples.ko: 이 사우나는 온탕이 두 개나 있어요.
examples.en: This sauna has as many as two hot baths.

explain: 대중목욕탕에서 따뜻한 물이 있는 탕을 말해요. 반대말은 '냉탕'이고, 보통 두 탕을 번갈아 이용해요. 집 욕조의 따뜻한 물에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Soaking in the hot bath relieves my tiredness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따뜻한 물에 몸을 푹 넣는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes sinking the body into warm water.
phrases.en_equiv: to soak in the hot bath

phrases.en: After the hot bath I got into the cold bath.
phrases.nuance_ko: 온탕의 반대말로, 찬물이 있는 탕이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 온탕: the bath with cold water.

phrases.en: I was cold, so I got into the hot bath first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목욕탕에서 따뜻한 탕으로 들어가는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the action of getting into the warm bath at a public bathhouse.
phrases.en_equiv: to get into the hot bath

explain_en: It refers to the pool with warm water in a public bathhouse. The opposite is '냉탕', and people often alternate between the two. It is not typically used for warm water in a home bathtub.

examples.ko: 항아리 주둥이가 좁아서 물을 붓기 어려워요.
examples.en: The jar's mouth is narrow, so it's hard to pour water in.
The bird pecked at the insect with its beak.

examples.ko: 강아지가 주둥이를 내 손에 갖다 댔어요.
examples.en: The puppy put its snout against my hand.
Steam is rising from the spout of the kettle.

examples.ko: 주둥이 끝이 뾰족한 새를 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever seen a bird with a pointed beak?

examples.ko: 병 주둥이를 입에 대고 마시지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't drink with your mouth on the bottle's opening.

explain: 새나 동물의 입 부분, 그리고 병이나 주전자처럼 좁게 튀어나온 입구를 가리킬 때 써요. 사람의 입에 쓰면 낮춰 부르는 말이라 무례하게 들리니 보통은 '입'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 병 주둥이가 좁아서 손이 안 들어가요.
phrases.en: The bottle's mouth is narrow, so my hand won't fit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 주전자의 좁은 입구를 말할 때 써요. 이럴 때는 무례하지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the narrow opening of a bottle or kettle; not rude in this use.

phrases.example: 저 새는 주둥이가 길어서 쉽게 알아봐요.
phrases.en: That bird has a long beak, so it's easy to recognize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새나 동물의 생김새를 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape of a bird's or animal's mouth.

phrases.en: My younger sibling laughed with their mouth wide open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 입에는 '주둥이' 대신 '입'을 써야 예의 바르게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people, use '입' instead of '주둥이' to sound polite.

explain_en: It is used for the mouth part of birds and animals, and for the narrow opening or spout of bottles and kettles. Using it for a person's mouth sounds rude and belittling, so people normally say '입'.

examples.en: I got hemorrhoids from sitting and working for a long time.
I had hemorrhoid surgery and rested for a week.
My hemorrhoids got worse, so I went to the hospital.
If you have constipation, you easily get hemorrhoids.

examples.ko: 아버지가 치질 때문에 오래 앉아 있기 힘들어하세요.
examples.en: My father has a hard time sitting for long because of hemorrhoids.

examples.ko: 치질은 부끄러워하지 말고 빨리 치료받아야 해요.
examples.en: Don't be embarrassed about hemorrhoids; get treated quickly.

explain: '양치질'의 '치질' 부분과 모양이 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉽지만 전혀 다른 말이에요. 이를 닦는 건 '양치질', 이건 항문의 병이에요. '치질에 걸리다/치질이 생기다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 오래 앉아 있으면 치질에 걸릴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you sit for a long time, you can get hemorrhoids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸린다는 뜻으로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The phrase for catching an illness.

phrases.en: I had bad constipation and developed hemorrhoids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 증상이 나타났다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like the condition appeared in the body.

phrases.en: The hemorrhoid surgery ended sooner than I expected.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병을 치료하는 방법으로 수술을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about surgery as a treatment for the condition.

explain_en: It looks like the last part of '양치질', so it is easy to mix up, but they are unrelated. Brushing teeth is '양치질', while this is a condition of the anus. You say '치질에 걸리다' or '치질이 생기다'.

en: to burp; to belch; to eruct

examples.en: The baby burped after drinking milk.
I burp often when I drink soda.
It is rude to burp during a meal.

examples.ko: 아기가 트림할 때까지 등을 두드려 주세요.
examples.en: Pat the baby's back until the baby burps.
After I burped, my stomach felt better.
I was embarrassed because I burped in front of a friend.

explain: 한국에서는 어른이 사람들 앞에서 트림하면 예의 없다고 느끼는 경우가 많아요. 반대로 아기는 우유를 먹은 뒤에 트림을 시켜 줘야 해서 '트림시키다'라는 말을 써요. '트림을 하다'라고 띄어 써도 뜻이 같아요.

phrases.en: I burped after eating and felt embarrassed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '트림하다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 이렇게 띄어서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '트림하다'; this spaced form is very common in speech.

phrases.en: I hold the baby and pat its back to make it burp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 트림하게 도와줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means helping a baby to burp, rather than burping yourself.

phrases.en: I drank sparkling water and now I keep burping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 일부러 하는 게 아니라 저절로 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the burp comes out on its own rather than on purpose.

explain_en: In Korea, burping in front of others as an adult is often seen as impolite. For babies, though, you help them burp after feeding, which is '트림시키다'. Writing '트림을 하다' with a space means the same.

examples.ko: 모기가 제 팔뚝을 여러 군데 물었어요.
examples.en: A mosquito bit my forearm in several places.
His forearms are thick and he is strong.
After I started exercising, my forearms became firm.
The nurse gave me an injection in my forearm.

examples.ko: 팔뚝 살을 빼고 싶어서 운동을 해요.
examples.en: I exercise because I want to lose arm fat.

examples.ko: 팔뚝에 큰 문신이 있는 사람이 지나갔어요.
examples.en: A person with a big tattoo on the forearm walked by.

explain: 팔꿈치와 손목 사이, 또는 어깨와 팔꿈치 사이 굵은 부분을 가리키는 일상적인 말이에요. 의학 용어로는 '아래팔', '위팔'로 나누지만 일상에서는 보통 '팔뚝' 하나로 말해요. '팔뚝 살'처럼 몸매 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 여름이 되면 팔뚝 살이 신경 쓰여요.
phrases.en: In summer I worry about my arm fat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸매 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about body shape.

phrases.en: I got a shot in my arm at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 주사 맞는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where you got a shot.
phrases.en_equiv: to get a shot in the arm

phrases.en: I fell and got a bruise on my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where you are hurt.
phrases.en_equiv: to get a bruise on the arm

explain_en: It is an everyday word for the thick part of the arm, between elbow and wrist or between shoulder and elbow. Medical terms separate 아래팔 and 위팔, but in daily life people just say 팔뚝. It often appears in body-shape talk, like 팔뚝 살.

en: to burn; to glow; to flush

examples.en: I sat in front of the heater and my face feels hot.
After eating spicy food, my mouth felt like it was burning.
I stayed in the sun a long time and my arms feel hot.

examples.ko: 사우나에서 나오자 온몸이 후끈거리는 느낌이 들었어요.
examples.en: When I came out of the sauna, my whole body felt flushed with heat.
I was so embarrassed that even my ears felt hot, so I lowered my head.
The room is stuffy and hot, so please open the window.

explain: 더운 기운이 확 올라오는 느낌을 말해요. 얼굴이나 몸이 뜨겁다고 할 때뿐 아니라 방 안의 열기에도 쓸 수 있어요. 피부가 쓰리거나 얼얼하면서 달아오르는 느낌은 '화끈거리다'가 더 잘 맞아요.

phrases.en: The room is warm and toasty after I turned on the heater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더운 기운이 느껴지는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where you feel hot air.

phrases.en: It is steaming hot inside the sauna.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열기가 계속 올라오는 느낌을 더 강하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses the feeling of heat continuously rising.

phrases.en: My arm burns because I got sunburned.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부가 쓰리고 달아오르는 느낌에 더 잘 맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits better for skin that stings and feels hot.

explain_en: It describes a rush of hot air or heat coming up, and can be used for your face or body as well as the heat in a room. When skin stings or tingles while burning up, '화끈거리다' fits better.
